title: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' Hits a Record 27th Week at No. 1 — and Takes a Second Mariah Carey Record With It
excerpt: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' holds the Billboard Hot 100 for a record 27th week, fending off Michael Jackson's 'Thriller' — and Dandelion just passed another Mariah Carey mark.
content:
On the Billboard Hot 100 dated November 14, Ella Langley's “Choosin' Texas” is No. 1 for a 27th week — the longest run at the top in the chart's history, which stretches back to August 1958. Billboard reported the new chart on Monday, November 9.

The song held the top on 18.8 million official streams, 53 million in radio audience and 4,000 sold in the tracking week of October 30 to November 5, according to Luminate data published by Billboard. It fended off a Halloween-powered surge from Michael Jackson's “Thriller,” which jumped from No. 20 to a new No. 2 peak, and Tame Impala and JENNIE's “Dracula,” which reached a new No. 3 high.

The record it broke

Mariah Carey's “All I Want for Christmas Is You” held the old record at 22 weeks at No. 1. Langley passed it in September, at 23 weeks, and has stretched the lead every week since. The 27 weeks are a total across seven separate runs since the song first reached No. 1 in February; its longest single stay was 14 straight weeks over the summer.

Langley co-wrote “Choosin' Texas” with Miranda Lambert, Luke Dick and Joybeth Taylor. Released in October 2025 as the lead single from her second album, Dandelion, it also leads Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart for a 48th week. Dandelion, released in April, opened at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

A second Carey record falls

The 27th week also moved a second long-standing Mariah Carey mark. Dandelion now stands as the female album with the most weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100 — 27 — passing Carey's Daydream, whose 26-week mark had stood for 30 years, according to Whiskey Riff's chart reporting on November 10. Carey set that album mark in 1995 with three No. 1 singles from Daydream; Langley reached 27 weeks with a single song.

Country radio, too

Radio is only half of Langley's week. Her follow-up single “Loving Life Again” is No. 1 on Mediabase's country chart and on Billboard's Country Airplay chart dated November 14, a second week on top there — making her the first woman in country radio history to hold two of the top three songs on the country panel at once. It is her seventh Mediabase No. 1 and the fourth No. 1 from Dandelion, after “Choosin' Texas,” “Be Her” and “I Can't Love You Anymore,” her duet with Morgan Wallen.

What it means

Analysis: Langley heads into the 60th CMA Awards on Wednesday, November 18, in Nashville as the year's most-nominated artist, with nine nominations including her first for Entertainer of the Year. The next Hot 100, dated November 21, will show whether “Choosin' Texas” reaches 28 weeks — or whether the longest reign in Hot 100 history closes here. Either way, the record now belongs to a 27-year-old from Alabama who told Billboard she knew “Choosin' Texas” was the lead single.

For country fans in Laredo and the 956, the CMA Awards air Wednesday, November 18, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+, streaming the next day on Hulu.
